recent_accepted.summary:
jev_decide.validate_response alone: ACCEPTS. requested="jev-1.13", returned="jev-1.13.2"; returned.startswith(requested+".") is True ("jev-1.13." prefix matches), so the regex+prefix check passes with no error.

However, Gateway.call also runs transport._validate_identity, which is stricter. For role=="jev" it normalizes the returned model to "typesafe/jev-1.13.2" and checks membership in config.response_models("jev", ...) = {"typesafe/jev-1.13", "typesafe/jev-1.13-20260917"}. "typesafe/jev-1.13.2" is not in that set, so require(...) fails and raises "response_model_mismatch".

Net result: the Gateway records error code "response_model_mismatch" for this call — identity validation rejects the response even though jev_decide's own validator would have let it through.

evidence.text: With default RunConfig, Gateway.call sends a valid Jev request for model "typesafe/jev-1.13". OpenRouter answers with model "jev-1.13.2" and otherwise valid usage, cost and answers. Would jev_decide.validate_response alone accept this model? What error code does the Gateway record for the call?

def _validate_identity(self, role, response, payload):
        returned = response.get("model")
        require(isinstance(returned, str), "missing_response_model")
        normalized = "typesafe/" + returned.removeprefix("typesafe/") if role == "jev" else returned
        require(normalized in self.config.response_models(role, payload["model"]), "response_model_mismatch")

requested = request["model"].removeprefix("~").removeprefix("typesafe/")
    returned = response["model"].removeprefix("typesafe/")
    require(re.fullmatch(r"jev-[A-Za-z0-9._-]+", returned) and
            (requested == "jev-latest" or returned == requested or
             returned.startswith((requested + ".", requested + "-"))), "response_model_mismatch")
